summary: St. Andrews North Point (Pendlebury Lighthouse): an 1833 wooden octagon kept by one family for almost a century, deactivated 1938, now a Civic Trust landmark.

light.note: Current light, on a skeletal tower about 75 m (250 ft) south of the 1833 tower (Coast Guard List of Lights; Rowlett). The 1833 tower's light was deactivated in 1938. Its first lighting date is not in the sources.

structures.type: octagonal wooden tower with lantern room
structures.note: Approx. 9 m (30 ft) octagonal pyramidal wood tower with lantern (Rowlett). The Canadian Register gives 13 m above high water; wood shingle cladding and eight windows with small panes in the lantern (Register; Civic Trust). Lantern room replaced in 2011 (Lighthouse Friends).
Current light tower with red and white rectangular daymark, 12.1 m structure height above ground (Coast Guard List of Lights).

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed. No parking at the lighthouse; park near Augustus and Patrick streets and walk south on Patrick Street (Lighthouse Friends).

events.note: Built on Indian Point at the eastern entrance to St. Andrews harbour, for £196 from the lighthouse fund
Keeper's dwelling built the following year
Lantern from Head Harbour Lighthouse placed atop the tower
Saxby Gale carried away part of the foundation block; wharf repairs
Gale of 23 November 1874 blew the tower over; no serious injury
Tower returned to its previous location after repair
Light decommissioned; last keeper Emma Pendlebury
Seawall partly collapsed in the early 1960s, tilting the tower; foundation shored up after an appeal by the Charlotte County Historical Society
Moved about fifty feet (15 m) in July 2002, off the deteriorating wharf
Ownership transferred to the St. Andrews Civic Trust
Lantern room removed and sent to a local community college for replication
Seawall rebuilt; tower restored and returned to its original location (Lighthouse Friends; the Register says a few metres from the original site)
Newly fabricated lantern room placed atop the tower on 24 October 2011

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikidata gives inactive; the Coast Guard list gives an active light (Fl R 4s); Rowlett says the 1833 tower has been inactive since 1938 with a separate active light offshore. Both are true: the tower is inactive and the modern light is active.

resolved_conflicts.field: keeper dates (John Pendlebury, George A. Pendlebury)
resolved_conflicts.explanation: Lighthouse Friends gives John Pendlebury 1842 to 1855 and George A. Pendlebury 1855 to 1889. The Canadian Register says John served until his death in 1853 and that George then operated the light. Both are kept, and the story says the sources differ.

Lighthouse Friends says the tower was returned to its original location in 2010. The Register says it sits only a few metres from its original site, and Rowlett describes a move of about 15 m in 2002 and a plan to return it. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Sources: Lighthouse Friends is the richest source and is copyrighted: the story paraphrases it and quotes only short phrases; the quotations it carries from the Commissioners and the 1876 Department report are cited as Lighthouse Friends reports them, since those reports are not in the local corpus (the corpus starts in fiscal 1900). The Canadian Register statement and the Civic Trust page give the same family history but disagree with Lighthouse Friends on John Pendlebury's end date (1853 against 1855). The Wikipedia article was read for leads only and is not cited. The Canadian Register listing date (2007) was only seen in a search snippet and is not used. Keeper lists: the 1905 list row 'Pendlebury, Wm. J ... St. Andrews ... April' was checked on the page image on 2026-10-28 (printed p. 261, scan 342): the name, station and appointment date (April 10, 1889) share a row, and the OCR name and station blocks each run to six entries in the same order. It is the only St. Andrews light with a Pendlebury keeper in the sources. The 1832 sum is printed with a garbled pound sign in the cached text; the story writes it as £784. The 1832 duties sentence now paraphrases Lighthouse Friends instead of quoting it. The 1909 keeper table prints 'W. J. Pendlebury' next to 'April 10, 1889' in column-split OCR. That agrees with Lighthouse Friends' 1889 start, but I matched it by adjacency only and did not use it. The 1902 wreck and obstruction table line 'Removed by John Pendlebury' names a John Pendlebury, but the station's John Pendlebury died in 1853 or 1855, so that line is not used and may be a different person. The 1907-08 repairs table line 'St. Andrew's point, repairs 75.00' is ambiguous (it could be this light or a range at the point) and is not used. The 1905 report's Navy Island lighthouse and the Navy Bar and Sand Reef lights are different structures and are not used. No Canadian newspaper archive was reachable, so the 1843, 1869 and 1874 events rest on Lighthouse Friends. Owners and staff in the 1960s and 2000s are named only by role and firm (Godin Ventures, Ltd.), not by person. The first lighting of the 1833 light is not in the sources, so first_lit is left out. The Register gives 13 m above high water (focal or structure height is unknown), while the record gives 9.0 m for the tower, and Rowlett gives 9 m (30 ft).
